# brainTrade Work Log

## 2026-08-10 02:29 UTC — [Pillar 3] KAITO episode archived as both decay gates fire

**Task:** Reapply the frozen KAITO archive gates—funding below 10 bps/hour or one-hour APR retention below 70% while recovery remains above 4.39 hours—and refresh the hedgeable extreme-funding candidate set.
**Finding:** KAITO funding fell from 12.0701 to 7.3799 bps/hour, a 38.86% one-hour decline and 61.14% retention. Both archive triggers fired. Although $1K paired depth improved slightly from 25.9937 to 25.5314 bps and basis compressed from -93.01 to -63.17 bps, fee-plus-depth of 54.5314 bps now needs 7.39 hours of funding before borrow and basis, materially worse than the 4.39-hour archive reference and latest 4.56-hour observation. Open interest recovered to $14.251M, but income decay dominates. JUP remains noncompetitive at 87.22 hours.
**My thinking:** Better liquidity, basis, and open interest cannot rescue an episode whose carry fell through both preregistered decay boundaries. Extending the sequence would create survivorship bias; a future KAITO extreme must begin a new persistence record.
**Decision:** Set `KAITO_EPISODE_ARCHIVED / FUNDING_7.38BPS_BELOW_10 / RETENTION_61.14PCT_BELOW_70 / RECOVERY_WIDENS_7.39H / JUP_REJECT_87.22H`. Close the observational episode, reset KAITO confirmation state for future research, and make no trade, borrow review, sizing, execution, live-configuration, or retired-bot change.
**Next:** Run a fresh candidate search next P3 heartbeat and treat any KAITO re-entry as snapshot one of a new episode; require funding persistence plus recovery improvement before restarting deeper cost analysis.
